Maria / Alex — adding a couple of legal clarifications from our side.

1) UK Addendum vs. UK IDTA: Our standard DPA includes SCC-based transfer clauses; for customers requiring an express UK IDTA addendum we provide a short addendum (UK Addendum) that references the UK Addendum text and the SCCs in Schedule A. For GlobeMed, the DPA Alex shared already has the addendum language populated in Annex 2. If you need our standalone IDTA form completed instead, we can do that — it will be an additional signature step.

2) Processor-to-processor transfers: If GlobeMed's use involves direct transfers to a subprocessor that is a separate data controller/processor (for example a downstream analytics partner), we treat that as a processor-supplied transfer in the subprocessor appendix and will notify you per the DPA notification windows.

3) Evidence granularity: We can provide a TIA summary that describes: legal basis used (SCC + UK Addendum), list of technical safeguards (TLS versions, at-rest encryption algo), and network topology notes. We typically do not provide raw logs or keys (obviously), but we can provide encryption key custody statements and KMS region details.

Next steps I propose:
- Alex: confirm whether GlobeMed needs a standalone UK IDTA or the embedded Addendum suffices (meeting procurement expectation).
- Hannah: can you confirm the KMS regions and whether the KV cache has any persistent copies outside EU/UK?

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Hi Maria — following up with the technical pack attached and a short checklist (see attached tia_summary_globemed_20270810.pdf). Summary highlights:

- Transfers/legal: We apply Standard Contractual Clauses (EU SCCs) by default and include the UK Addendum language for UK customers. The DPA Alex shared includes the UK language; if you prefer the separate UK IDTA we can prepare it for signature.
- Encryption: TLS 1.2+ in transit; AES-256 at rest for customer data. Keys are stored in a customer-isolated KMS instance per Dedicated/Private deployments. For Hosted customers keys are in our KMS with HSM-backed key wrapping; KMS region is currently eu-west-1 for EU customers by default (can be pinned on Dedicated).
- Subprocessors and KV cache: The subprocessor map notes two vendors that perform indexing and analytics and may temporarily process derivatives in us-east-1 for batch processing; no persistent primary data copies are retained outside EU/UK for customer-managed Dedicated deployments. For Hosted accounts we provide contractual assurances and a notification process for subprocessor changes.
- Mitigations we recommend: pin KMS region (if regulatory requirement), include explicit Data Residency clause in SOW, and request a periodic subprocessor attestation (we can provide quarterly snapshots).

Attached artifacts: tia_summary_globemed_20270810.pdf (TIA summary & checklist), referenced subprocessor_map_20270803.xlsx, Redwood_DPA_Signed_GM_20270803.pdf

Related links:
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/GM-2027-85
- Completed Docusign: https://app.docusign.com/documents/XYZ-GLM-2027

If GlobeMed's legal team wants the standalone UK IDTA, Alex — let me know and I'll coordinate the internal sign-off path (should be quick). Otherwise we can mark this as "Addendum included" and proceed with procurement.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Security & Compliance Lead
Redwood Inference
